instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get total salary of all employees
output: SELECT SUM(salary) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get average salary
output: SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get highest salary
output: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get lowest salary
output: SELECT MIN(salary) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Count total employees
output: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Count employees per department
output: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get average salary per department
output: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Get departments with average salary above 60000
output: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 60000;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total, status)
Get total revenue from completed orders
output: SELECT SUM(total) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total, status)
Get average order value per user
output: SELECT user_id, AVG(total) FROM orders GROUP BY user_id;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total, status)
Get users with more than 3 orders
output: SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, price, category)
Get the most expensive product per category
output: SELECT category, MAX(price) FROM products GROUP BY category;

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, price, category)
Get categories with more than 10 products
output: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 10;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, grade)
Get average GPA per grade
output: SELECT grade, AVG(gpa) FROM students GROUP BY grade;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, grade)
Get the minimum GPA in each grade
output: SELECT grade, MIN(gpa) FROM students GROUP BY grade;

instruction:
Schema: sales(id, product_id, amount, sale_date)
Get total sales per month
output: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date) AS month, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date);

instruction:
Schema: sales(id, product_id, amount, sale_date)
Get total sales per year
output: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sale_date) AS year, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sale_date);

instruction:
Schema: logs(id, level, message, created_at)
Count logs per level
output: SELECT level, COUNT(*) FROM logs GROUP BY level;

instruction:
Schema: logs(id, level, message, created_at)
Get the date of the earliest error log
output: SELECT MIN(created_at) FROM logs WHERE level = 'error';

instruction:
Schema: inventory(id, product_id, quantity, warehouse)
Get total quantity per warehouse
output: SELECT warehouse, SUM(quantity) FROM inventory GROUP BY warehouse;

instruction:
Schema: inventory(id, product_id, quantity, warehouse)
Get warehouses with less than 100 total items
output: SELECT warehouse, SUM(quantity) FROM inventory GROUP BY warehouse HAVING SUM(quantity) < 100;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, salary, department_id)
Count distinct salaries
output: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT salary) FROM employees;

instruction:
Schema: transactions(id, account_id, amount, type)
Get total deposits per account
output: SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE type = 'deposit' GROUP BY account_id;

instruction:
Schema: transactions(id, account_id, amount, type)
Get total withdrawals per account
output: SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE type = 'withdrawal' GROUP BY account_id;

instruction:
Schema: reviews(id, product_id, rating, review_text)
Get average rating per product
output: SELECT product_id, AVG(rating) FROM reviews GROUP BY product_id;
